name: Sign the agreement
teaching: The agreement sets the terms for our work together. Once it's signed, we're official — and the work begins.
howTo: Done when: the agreement is signed, dated, and submitted back through the signature platform. You've received a copy in your email.

name: Make your first payment
teaching: First payment locks in your spot. No payment, no build. That's how we keep the energy serious.
howTo: Done when: your first payment has cleared and shows up in the payment platform. You've received a receipt by email.

name: Complete your onboarding form
teaching: This form pulls out everything I need to build your system right. Your offer, your audience, your existing assets, your baseline numbers. Spend time on this — it sets the tone for everything.
howTo: Done when: every question on the onboarding form is answered honestly and submitted. No placeholders. No "I'll fill that in later."

name: Choose where your community will live
teaching: Your community needs a home. Facebook Group. Skool. Circle. Slack. Pick one. Don't overthink it — you can always move later.
howTo: Done when: you've chosen one community platform and posted your choice and reasoning in the Evolve Omega community.

name: Confirm your GoHighLevel access
teaching: GHL is the engine room. It's where your leads, automations, and pipelines live. You need to be able to get in.
howTo: Done when: you're logged into GoHighLevel with your own password, 2FA is on, the dashboard is bookmarked, and you've posted a screenshot in the community.

name: Confirm your HelixOS access
teaching: HelixOS is your command center. This is where you track your pathway, see your points, and stay organized.
howTo: Done when: you've logged into HelixOS, bookmarked your Success Pathway dashboard, and posted a screenshot in the community.

name: Schedule your kickoff call
teaching: The kickoff call is where we align on your 90-day plan. This is the moment we move from setup to execution.
howTo: Done when: the kickoff call is booked on both calendars, the Zoom link is confirmed, and you've prepped using the 48-hour note.

name: Film "Start Here" Video
teaching: A clear Start Here video is recorded and placed in the community so every new member knows where to begin, what the community is for, and what action to take first.
howTo: Done when: a Start Here video under 3 minutes is recorded, uploaded, pinned or featured, and tested from the member side. A 6-month re-record reminder is set.

name: Create Rules & Standards Page
teaching: Create a clear Rules & Standards page that sets expectations and creates a safe, high-quality community environment.
howTo: Done when: a Rules & Standards page with 5–7 specific rules is published and pinned in the group, linked from the welcome message, and screenshotted in HelixOS.

name: Write Leverage Question (Data Capture)
teaching: A high-value qualifying question is written and embedded in group membership questions to capture lead intelligence on join.
howTo: Done when: your leverage question is live as a Facebook Group membership question. Answers are flowing into a tracked system you review weekly.

name: Create Public Welcome Post Template
teaching: A reusable welcome post template exists that publicly celebrates new members joining the group, increasing belonging and early engagement.
howTo: Done when: a welcome post template is saved in HelixOS with a name placeholder, a warm welcome line, and a specific CTA. A posting cadence is set.

name: Install Auto-Welcome Tagging Process
teaching: A process is in place to automatically or semi-automatically tag and welcome new members when they join the group.
howTo: Done when: a new member gets auto-tagged and receives a personalized welcome message within 24 hours of joining. A segmentation tag is also being applied based on the leverage question.

name: Define Community Posting Guidelines
teaching: Clear posting guidelines are written and published in the group so members know what is and is not allowed, reducing moderation workload.
howTo: Done when: 5 posting guidelines are written, published as a pinned post or in the group description, and referenced in the welcome post.

name: Create a safe test contact process
teaching:
Outcome: Client can test without affecting real users

Create a testing routine using preview/test contacts before publishing or sending real traffic.

Why this matters: This task helps a beginner business owner build a safe, measurable Community Loyalty system for generating, nurturing, and converting leads.
howTo:
Create a testing routine using preview/test contacts before publishing or sending real traffic.

Success criteria: Every flow can be tested before it affects prospects.

Verification: Run one preview interaction and confirm the user record updates as expected.
unlocks: Every flow can be tested before it affects prospects.

name: Install No-Spam Enforcement SOP
teaching: A no-spam enforcement process is documented and implemented so that spam is consistently identified and removed without debate.
howTo: Done when: the No-Spam SOP is written with 3 steps (identify, action, document), shared with every mod, and a spam log exists where removals are tracked.

name: Create your New Member Welcome Roll Call post
teaching: A pinned welcome post invites new members to introduce themselves, increasing early engagement and community belonging.
howTo: Done when: a Welcome Roll Call post is published and pinned, every introduction gets a personal reply within 24 hours, and a 30-day refresh reminder is set.

name: Set up your Start Here post with 5 onboarding steps for new members
teaching: New members land on a clear, structured Start Here post that guides them through the first 5 actions to take in the community.
howTo: Done when: a Start Here post with 5 numbered steps is published, pinned, and linked from the welcome automation. Every link in it is live and tested.

name: Set up your Featured Posts to anchor key content at the top of your group
teaching: Key community content (Start Here, rules, offers) is anchored at the top of the group so all members can find it immediately.
howTo: Done when: exactly 3 featured posts are live at the top of the group (Start Here, Rules, Current Offer/Event), each has a graphic cover, and a 30-day rotation reminder is set.

name: Learn how to approve posts the right way using your admin dashboard
teaching: Admin is confident approving, declining, and flagging posts using the Facebook admin dashboard to maintain community quality.
howTo: Done when: a daily pending-post review block is on your calendar, a documented approval standard exists and is shared with all mods, and you've reviewed at least 5 pending posts using the dashboard.

name: Create a system to identify and engage new members on their first post (wave emoji)
teaching: Create a system that identifies new members by the wave emoji and triggers immediate engagement on their first post.
howTo: Done when: a daily wave-emoji check ritual is on your calendar, a documented response protocol exists in HelixOS, and at least one new member has been engaged using the protocol.

name: Explore the chatbot dashboard and understand the Omni-channel panel
teaching: Student has navigated all key sections of the Community Loyalty dashboard and understands the Omni-channel panel layout and functionality.
howTo: Done when: every section of the chatbot dashboard has been explored, a 1-sentence cheat sheet is saved in HelixOS, and the Omni-channel panel is understood well enough to explain what lives where.

name: Build your chatbot welcome sequence and personalized greeting flow
teaching: Every new subscriber to the chatbot receives a personalized welcome sequence that introduces the brand and sets expectations.
howTo: Done when: a 3-message chatbot welcome sequence is live with first-name personalization, 24–48 hour spacing, and has been tested end-to-end with a test subscriber.

name: Learn to use Airtable views to customize your workflow dashboard
teaching: Student can create and use custom Airtable views to filter, sort, and organize their data to match their workflow needs.
howTo: Done when: at least 2 custom Airtable views are created, clearly named, filtered to show only what matters, and actively used in your weekly workflow.

name: Collect and organize brand assets
teaching: Student gathers the client’s logos, colors, fonts, links, photos, testimonials, and offer assets into one organized workspace.
howTo: Done when: a complete asset folder exists in HelixOS with all required materials clearly labeled and organized by category. The folder is shared with the build team.

name: Request missing access and implementation assets
teaching: Student identifies missing tools, logins, assets, or approvals and sends a complete access request to the client or internal team.
howTo: Done when: a complete missing-items request has been sent with specific items and a deadline, and every received asset is logged in HelixOS.

name: Build internal offer brief
teaching: Student translates the client’s offer into a clear internal brief that the implementation team can build from accurately.
howTo: Done when: a 2–3 page offer brief exists in HelixOS with all 9 sections completed (promise, audience, pricing, objections, belief shifts, bonuses, CTA, FAQs, conversion path) and has been walked through with the build team.

name: Map the customer journey from entry to purchase
teaching: Student creates a full omnichannel journey map from content entry point to registration, nurture, event attendance, offer invitation, and follow-up.
howTo: Done when: a complete journey map exists in HelixOS showing every step from first touch to post-purchase, with channel, trigger, action, and outcome labeled for each step.

name: Identify objections and belief shifts
teaching: Student identifies the major objections, false beliefs, and mindset shifts that the funnel and messaging must address to convert.
howTo: Done when: 3 objections and 3 belief shifts are documented in HelixOS, each written in the prospect's own language, and each mapped to a specific funnel touchpoint.

name: Prepare cross-channel messaging sheet
teaching: Student prepares a messaging sheet that keeps headlines, CTAs, proof, and positioning consistent across pages, chatbot, email, SMS, and reminders.
howTo: Done when: a complete messaging sheet exists in HelixOS with headline, subhead, CTA, objection responses, proof themes, and channel-specific notes. The sheet is shared with the full launch team.

name: Build registration confirmation workflow
teaching: Student builds the workflow that handles registration confirmations, tagging, reminders, and internal notifications.
howTo: Done when: a registration workflow in GHL fires on form submit and successfully sends the confirmation email, applies the tag, updates the pipeline, and notifies the internal team. A test registration confirms every step.

name: Load email confirmation sequence
teaching: Student loads the registration confirmation emails with the correct copy, links, and timing.
howTo: Done when: the confirmation email template is built, triggers within 5 minutes of registration, every link works, merge fields populate correctly, and a test email has been successfully received and reviewed on mobile and desktop.

name: Write your lead magnet
teaching: Your lead magnet is the first thing your ideal lead touches. It has to solve one real problem — fast. Not everything. One thing.
howTo: Write the name, promise, and outline of your lead magnet. Keep it focused. Post your draft in the community for feedback.

name: Set your price point
teaching: Your price signals value. Too cheap and people don't take it seriously. Too expensive without the positioning and nobody buys. Pick a number that matches the transformation.
howTo: Pick your price. Write 2–3 sentences defending it. Post in the community.

name: Decide how buyers get onboarded
teaching: The moment someone buys is the moment they're most excited. Waste that moment and you've created buyer's remorse. Nail it and you've created a raving fan.
howTo: Sketch out what happens in the first 24 hours after someone buys. Welcome email? Kickoff call? Access link? Post your plan in the community.

name: Prepare bonuses or fast-action incentives
teaching: A clean offer converts. A clean offer with a reason to act now converts better. Not fake scarcity — real reasons to decide today.
howTo: List 1–3 bonuses OR 1 fast-action incentive OR 1 real scarcity element. Explain why each is valuable. Post in the community.

name: Install 3 Membership Questions
teaching: Three strategic membership questions are installed in the Facebook group to qualify, engage, and capture data from every new member request.
howTo:
- Write Micro-Commitment Question (Irrefutable Yes)
- Write Support-Based Offer Question
- Write Leverage Question (Data Capture)

name: Film your welcome live in your facebook group!
teaching: A welcome live is recorded inside the Facebook group so new members feel personally welcomed, oriented, and invited into early participation.
howTo:
- Welcome live has been recorded inside the Facebook group
- Live includes a welcome, orientation, and participation invitation
- Replay is visible in the group for new members to watch
- Screenshot or replay link is saved

name: Define Moderator Engagement Expectations
teaching: Written expectations for moderator engagement frequency, response time, and interaction style are defined and shared.
howTo: Written document outlines at least 5 moderator responsibilities with clear daily/weekly expectations.

name: Create Moderator Morning Ritual
teaching: Moderators have a documented morning routine that ensures consistent daily group health, engagement, and activity.
howTo: Morning ritual checklist is written with at least 5 steps. At least one moderator has completed the ritual for 3+ consecutive days.

name: Define Ideal Client Criteria
teaching: Define the exact criteria that identify your ideal client so you can focus your energy on the right prospects.
howTo:
- Ideal client is described demographically and psychographically
- Pain points and desires are documented
- Disqualifying factors are listed
- Criteria are saved in Airtable or a doc

name: Build Qualification Questions in Chatbot
teaching: Qualification questions are built into the chatbot flow to screen prospects and identify their readiness, budget, and fit before human follow-up.
howTo: At least 5 qualification questions are live in the chatbot. Bot correctly routes answers to the appropriate follow-up path.

name: Install Lead Tracking System
teaching: A lead tracking system is installed and in use so all prospects are logged, staged, and followed up with consistently.
howTo: Lead tracking system (Airtable, CRM, or equivalent) is active with at least 10 leads entered and staged correctly.

name: Create Bridge Invitation Post Template
teaching: A bridge invitation post template exists to invite warm leads from other groups into your own community in a non-spammy, value-first way.
howTo: Template is written with value hook, social proof, and invitation CTA. Template has been tested or is ready to deploy.

name: Install Sales Tracking Dashboard
teaching: A sales tracking dashboard is live that shows pipeline stage, follow-up status, and revenue metrics in one view.
howTo: Dashboard is set up with at least pipeline stages, lead count per stage, and close rate. Data is being actively updated.

name: Install Monthly Metrics Review
teaching: Install a monthly metrics review process that keeps your community performance data visible and actionable.
howTo:
\- Monthly review date is set on calendar
\- Metrics to review are identified
\- Review template or checklist is created

name: Define Rank Thresholds
teaching: Establish clear point thresholds that define rank progression within your community.
howTo:
'- Rank levels are named and documented (e.g. Newcomer, Contributor, Leader)
\- Point thresholds for each rank are defined and recorded
\- Criteria are visible or accessible to members
\- Thresholds are entered into your tracking system

name: Define Community Core Values
teaching: 3-5 non-negotiable community core values are defined and documented to guide behavior, content, and moderation standards.
howTo: 3-5 core values are written with a short description of each. Values are accessible to members and used in onboarding.

name: Define Community Identity Language
teaching: Unique community identity language (group name for members, signature phrases, shared vocabulary) is defined to build belonging.
howTo: At least 3 identity language elements are defined (e.g., what members are called, a rallying phrase, a community hashtag).

name: Create Conversation-to-Conversion Bridge Posts
teaching: Create posts that bridge organic community conversation to offer conversion.
howTo:
\- At least 3 bridge post templates are written
\- Posts transition smoothly from conversation to offer
\- Templates are saved in content library

name: Define Soft Qualification Signals
teaching: Define what behaviors indicate buying readiness among community members.
howTo:

\- At least 5 buying-readiness behaviors or patterns are identified
\- Signals are linked to follow-up or sales decision logic
\- Document is saved where moderators or sales team can use it

name: Define Participation KPI Target %
teaching: Set and document the target participation rate percentage for the community.
howTo:
\- KPI or metric is identified and tracked
\- Data source is confirmed
\- Current baseline is documented
\- Tracking method is in place

name: Define Activation Rate %
teaching: Define and document the target activation rate percentage for new members.
howTo:
\- Activation rate target percentage is defined and documented
\- Formula for measuring activation is clear
\- Data source for tracking activation is identified
\- Target and baseline are saved in the KPI system

name: Define Webinar KPI Targets

howTo: At least 3 post templates are fully customized with your logo, colors, and fonts. Templates are saved and accessible.

name: Build your first subflow as a navigation roadmap for prospects

howTo: Subflow is live in the chatbot builder with at least 3 navigation branches. Test run confirms all paths work correctly.

name: Set up automations and triggers to start conversations with prospects

howTo: At least 2 automation triggers are active. Each trigger fires correctly when the test condition is met and starts the right conversation flow.

name: Create a follow-up sequence to keep conversations going after opt-in

name: Set up Airtable linking to connect your tables (leads, tasks, offers, etc.)
teaching: Airtable tables are linked so related data flows between them automatically, creating a connected CRM and ops system.
howTo: At least 2 tables are linked with a relationship field. A test record in one table references a correct linked record in another table.

name: Use the Airtable Web Clipper to capture prospect data from the web

howTo: Web Clipper extension is installed. At least one prospect record has been clipped from a webpage and saved to the correct Airtable table.

teaching: Student has a defined list of 3-5 high-value Facebook groups where ideal clients are active and where lead generation activity will be focused.
howTo: Written list of 3-5 groups with group name, member count, engagement level, and reason for selection. At least 2 groups have been joined.

howTo: Team member appears in Page Roles with the correct access level. They have confirmed access and can log in to manage the page.

howTo: Tracker includes all major phases from onboarding through launch, with owners, dates, dependencies, and status visibility.

teaching: Student builds a branded registration page that captures leads and clearly communicates the event or offer invitation.
howTo: Page is branded, mobile responsive, connected to the form or CRM, and contains headline, promise, proof, CTA, and confirmation flow.

name: Build thank-you and confirmation pages
teaching: Student builds the next-step pages that confirm registration and direct the lead toward attendance and engagement.
howTo: Thank-you and confirmation pages are live, mobile ready, properly linked, and contain event access instructions and next steps.

name: Connect forms and buttons across funnel
teaching: Student connects all funnel buttons, forms, redirects, and calendars so the user journey works end to end.
howTo: Every primary CTA, form submission, redirect, and calendar action has been tested and routes correctly.

name: Create CRM pipeline stages
teaching: Student creates or cleans the CRM pipeline so leads can be tracked clearly from first contact through conversion and fulfillment.
howTo: Pipeline stages are live, logically ordered, and aligned with the actual customer journey.

name: Build comment-to-DM trigger flow
teaching: Student connects social post engagement to the DM conversation entry experience using the right keyword or trigger logic.
howTo: A qualifying comment or keyword starts the intended DM flow and applies the correct routing and follow-up logic.

name: Tag and route leads by chatbot answers
teaching: Student applies tags, internal routing, or next-step destinations based on chatbot responses and lead quality.
howTo: Each major answer path applies the intended tag or routing action and updates the lead record correctly.

name: Connect webinar registration to CRM and reminders
teaching: Student connects webinar registration so every registrant is captured, tagged, and entered into the correct reminder flow.
howTo: A test registrant appears in the CRM with the correct tag and automatically receives the webinar reminder workflow.

name: Prepare promo content calendar
teaching: Student prepares the promo content calendar so invitation posts align with the live funnel and campaign dates.
howTo: A dated content calendar exists with post themes, CTAs, trigger keywords, and launch timing aligned to the backend system.

name: Prepare CTA copy and comment trigger instructions
teaching: Student prepares the CTA language and trigger instructions that move content viewers into the DM or registration flow.
howTo: Each content asset includes the correct CTA wording, keyword, and routing instructions for the intended entry path.

name: Track leads generated by campaign
teaching: Student tracks how many leads the campaign generated across the active entry points.
howTo: A reporting view or sheet shows total leads generated and clearly identifies the campaign or traffic source.

name: Track purchase and conversion rate
teaching: Student measures how many qualified leads converted into buyers and reports the overall conversion rate.
howTo: A report exists showing total buyers, total qualified leads or registrants, and the resulting conversion rate.

name: Create Custom Forms & Integrate Them into Your Funnel Pages
teaching: Build a custom lead capture form in GoHighLevel with required fields (name, phone, email), consent/terms checkbox, and a submit button — then embed it into a funnel page so prospects can register for events, book calls, or opt in to your offers.
howTo:
1\. A new form is created in GoHighLevel Sites > Forms with a descriptive, event-specific name (e.g., 'March Webinar 2025 Form').
2\. Required fields are configured: First Name, Last Name, Phone (with country picker if needed), and Email — all marked as required.
3\. A consent/terms & conditions checkbox is included with proper verbiage and linked privacy policy/terms of service URLs.
4\. The submit button text is customized to match the CTA (e.g., 'Secure My Seat').
5\. The form is embedded into a funnel page using the funnel editor's Add Element > Form feature.
6\. The form's post-submission action is configured (go to next step, redirect to URL, or thank you page).
7\. The form is previewed and tested to confirm all fields capture data correctly.

name: Build a Basic Email Automation Workflow with Form Trigger, Tags, Pipeline & Confirmation Email
teaching: Create a GoHighLevel automation workflow that triggers when a prospect submits a form, adds a tracking tag, creates a pipeline opportunity, sets a lead source, and sends a branded confirmation email — establishing the foundational automation sequence for event registrations and lead nurturing.
howTo:
1\. A new workflow is created in GoHighLevel Automations with a clear, descriptive name.
2\. The workflow trigger is set to 'Form Submitted' and filtered to a specific form.
3\. A descriptive tag (e.g., 'LYC-registered') is added to contacts who trigger the workflow.
4\. A pipeline opportunity is created with the correct pipeline and stage selected.
5\. Lead source is set on the contact record to track where they came from.
6\. A confirmation email action is added with a personalized subject line, the contact's first name via custom field picker, event details, and clear next-step instructions.
7\. The workflow is toggled ON (published) and tested with a test form submission.
8\. The contact record is verified to show the tag, pipeline entry, and email delivery.

name: Launch a New Outreach Project: Gather Prospect Insights & Plan Your Conversion Campaign
teaching: Kick off a new outreach project by surveying your community or prospect list to gather insights about their problems, pains, and desires — then use that data to plan a targeted conversion campaign to turn prospects into clients.
howTo:
1\. Your prospect list is identified and quantified (e.g., 1,700+ contacts in your community).
2\. A survey or outreach method has been used to gather insights about prospects' problems, pains, and desires.
3\. The gathered data is organized and reviewed to identify common themes and patterns.
4\. A conversion campaign plan is documented based on the prospect insights.
5\. Outreach has begun with personalized messaging that addresses the identified pain points.

name: Implement Conditional Logic (If/Then Branches) in GoHighLevel Workflows
teaching: Add conditional logic (If/Then branches) to your GoHighLevel workflows to create different automation paths based on contact properties like tags, custom fields, or VIP status — using clear naming conventions for each condition and branch for maintainability.
howTo:
1\. A workflow includes at least one If/Then conditional logic step that branches contacts based on specific criteria (e.g., tag = VIP vs. non-VIP).
2\. Each conditional action is named descriptively (e.g., 'Check if Contact is VIP') instead of using generic names like 'Condition'.
3\. Both the YES and NO branches have appropriate follow-up actions configured.
4\. Tags are used effectively to differentiate contact segments within the workflow.
5\. Advanced conditional logic with multiple branches is demonstrated for more complex scenarios.
6\. The workflow is tested with contacts that match different conditions to verify correct branch routing.

name: Clean Up & Manage Your Chatbot Subscriber List (Filter, Delete Non-Prospects & Upgrade Capacity)
teaching: Maintain a clean and optimized chatbot subscriber list by filtering out non-prospects, removing inactive subscribers who have never messaged you, and understanding upgrade options for increasing your bot user capacity when your list grows.
howTo:
1\. Bot subscriber list has been reviewed and filtered using the 'Last Text Input is empty' filter to identify non-engaged subscribers.
2\. Non-prospect and inactive subscribers have been selected and deleted from the bot list.
3\. Student understands the bot user capacity tiers (1,000 default, 2,000 for $20, 10,000 for $50) and knows how to request an upgrade if needed.
4\. Subscriber list only contains active prospects and engaged contacts.

name: Set up your community platform
teaching: This is the digital home. Name it, brand it, make it feel like a real place — not an empty room.

name: Define your community's purpose and promise

name: Invite your warm audience

name: Identify people to engage with early

name: Post a win or challenge (weekly)
teaching: Communities live on stories. Your wins inspire others. Your challenges make space for help.
howTo: Post at least one win or challenge per week in the Academy community.

name: Bring one question to each call (weekly)
teaching: Passive attendance is shallow. One good question transforms the call.
howTo: Bring one question or obstacle to each Academy call. Post it in the community beforehand if possible.

name: Review HelixOS KPIs (monthly)
teaching: What you don't look at, you can't change. Monthly review is the minimum.
howTo: Review your KPIs in HelixOS monthly. Post one insight or trend in our community.

name: Set a quarterly revenue goal
teaching: Without a quarterly goal, you drift. With one, you aim.
howTo: Set your quarterly revenue or growth goal. Post it in our community with your plan.

name: Share testimonials as they happen
teaching: Social proof compounds. Share wins as they come — don't wait.
howTo: Share a testimonial, case study, or client win in our community as they happen.

name: Identify when you're ready for Elite or Luxe
teaching: There's a moment you outgrow Academy. Notice it. Don't stay stuck.
howTo: When you feel you've outgrown Academy's pace, reach out to discuss Elite or Luxe. Post a "I'm considering levelling up" note.

name: Install Client Success Tracking System
teaching: A system is in place to track active client progress, milestones, and satisfaction so no client feels unsupported.
howTo: Client tracking system is active with all current clients entered. Each record includes start date, milestones, and next action.

name: Define Client Milestone Markers
teaching: Clear milestone markers are defined for client journeys so progress can be measured, celebrated, and used as proof points.
howTo: At least 5 milestone markers are defined with criteria for each. Milestones are mapped to the client journey phases.

name: Install Points System
teaching: A points-based reward system is installed and active to gamify participation and incentivize ongoing member engagement.
howTo: Points system is configured with at least 5 point-earning actions defined. At least one member has earned points since launch.

name: Complete All OS Stages
teaching: Complete all Operating System stages to demonstrate full mastery of the community business model.
howTo:
\- All OS stages are marked complete in Airtable
\- Evidence has been submitted for each stage
\- Coach has reviewed and approved your progress
\- You are ready to submit for final certification

name: Pass OS Audit Review
teaching: Pass the OS Audit Review to demonstrate mastery of all Operating System stages.
howTo:
\- All required OS stages have been completed
\- Audit review has been submitted
\- Feedback from coach or reviewer has been received
\- Pass status is confirmed

name: Record Community Walkthrough Loom
teaching: Record a Loom walkthrough of your full community setup as certification evidence.
howTo:
\- System or structure is built and documented
\- All required components are in place
\- Setup confirmed with Loom walkthrough
\- Available and accessible to relevant parties

name: Pass Structured Audit Review
teaching: Complete and pass the structured audit review to achieve certification.
howTo:
\- All audit criteria have been reviewed
\- Submission is prepared and sent to coach
\- Feedback has been received
\- Pass confirmation is documented

name: Create your Pass Type IDs for community loyalty passes (A to Z setup)
teaching: All required Pass Type IDs are created and configured in the loyalty pass system, enabling the full A-to-Z loyalty pass workflow.
howTo: Pass Type IDs are created in the loyalty platform. Each pass type has a name, ID, and at minimum one field configured. Test pass can be issued.

name: Build no-show and replay workflows
teaching: Student creates automated paths for no-shows, replays, and next-step follow-up after the live event.
howTo: No-show contacts are segmented correctly and receive the replay and follow-up sequence without manual intervention.

name: Test every chatbot branch
teaching: Student runs test scenarios through each major chatbot branch and verifies the logic, copy, and routing behavior.
howTo: Every key path has been tested, bugs are logged or fixed, and the tested outcomes are documented clearly.

name: Verify mobile rendering for core emails
teaching: Student checks how the confirmation, reminder, and follow-up emails appear on mobile devices.
howTo: Core emails are readable, correctly formatted, and free of broken layout issues on mobile.

name: Test pass install experience on device
teaching: Student tests the full install and display experience of the pass on an actual supported device.
howTo: The pass installs successfully, displays correctly, and all major interactions work on a real device.

name: Verify content and funnel alignment
teaching: Student checks that front-end content promises, CTAs, and entry points match the live funnel experience exactly.
howTo: The message, CTA, trigger, and destination are consistent between the post, DM path, registration page, and follow-up flow.

name: Test every funnel form and page link
teaching: Student tests every page link, form, redirect, and user action in the active funnel before launch.
howTo: Each form and link is tested successfully and any broken action is fixed or documented before go-live.

name: Log and resolve launch bugs
teaching: Student logs issues found during QA or launch and works through resolution in a methodical way.
howTo: Each issue is documented with root cause, fix status, and retest result before the launch is marked ready.

name: Provide implementation status updates
teaching: Student communicates clear status updates to the client or strategist so progress stays visible and trust remains high.
howTo: A concise status update shows what is complete, what is in progress, what is blocked, and what is needed next.

name: Summarize next steps after implementation call
teaching: Student summarizes decisions and next steps clearly after a call so there is no confusion about ownership or timing.
howTo: Call summary includes decisions made, deliverables, owners, dates, and unresolved questions.

name: Fix page links, form mapping, and notification errors
teaching: Student resolves common implementation errors such as broken links, bad field mapping, and missed internal notifications.
howTo: The identified issue is fixed, retested successfully, and documented so the error does not recur unnoticed.

name: Simplify chatbot or form friction points
teaching: Student simplifies unnecessary friction inside the chatbot or forms to improve completion rates.
howTo: The friction point is identified, the flow is simplified, and the revised experience is tested successfully.

Success criteria: Points actions match the business rules.

Verification: Run a test points event and inspect the points ledger.
unlocks: Points actions match the business rules.

name: Run final pre-launch test
teaching:
Outcome: Client can launch safely

Run the full journey from entry point through data capture, branching, follow-up, conversion, AI/handoff if used, and reporting.

Why this matters: This task helps a beginner business owner build a safe, measurable Community Loyalty system for generating, nurturing, and converting leads.
howTo:
Run the full journey from entry point through data capture, branching, follow-up, conversion, AI/handoff if used, and reporting.

Success criteria: The flow works end to end before real traffic.

Verification: Complete a test interaction and verify messages, fields, tags, notifications, and dashboard metrics.
unlocks: The flow works end to end before real traffic.
